correctness.rationale: The original four equations imply D²=0 and BD=DB=CD=DC=0, forcing a three-block factor form. Multiplication gives precisely disjoint injective columns and four annihilating constraints that identify both middle endomorphisms with a zero-product pair on W=ker P∩ker U of dimension b=n−4t. Counting injections, graph lifts, P/U extensions, and arbitrary extreme blocks yields q^(3t²+2tb) I(a,t) I(a−t,t) Z_b(q). The two independent subspace-lattice Möbius inversions count the residual Z_b(q) without overcounting. All cases, including characteristic two, t=0 and 4t>n, follow. A standalone program independently exhausts selected small zero-product spaces and the entire n=4,t=1,q=2 nonzero fiber against the original matrix identities. A second original-identity check tests all 672 parametrized factorizations of a rank-one five-dimensional binary target.

originality.rationale: The all-dimensional, all-prime-power nonzero product-fiber formula is compared against the closest published existence theorem of Kokol Bukovšek–Košir–Novak–Oblak, Levy geometric studies and Britnell–Wildon commuting-class results. The previously computed 4×4 fiber and the zero-product count are credited as known; neither contains the all-dimensional factorization-fiber bijection or its multiplicative formula. value.rationale: The product image of commuting square-zero matrices is a natural and explicitly studied matrix-factorization problem. The new multiplicative fiber theorem determines the exact labeled preimage cardinality for every matrix D, in every dimension and finite-field characteristic, extending a known n=4 slice. It supplies a global, closed, computable arithmetic census beyond the existing yes/no image classification and beyond the known unrefined zero-product flags; no arbitrary numerical cutoff is built into the claim.
